concepts.definition: Surface-dwelling future humans whose language differs from that of the underground beings.

concepts.label: Precipice_of_despair_metaphor

concepts.label: Creator_self_dedication_to_destruction_mission

concepts.definition: The creature’s last address to the dead Frankenstein, claiming he will see no more humans and contrasting their sufferings.
concepts.evidence_quote: “Farewell! I leave you, and in you the last of humankind whom these eyes will ever behold. Farewell, Frankenstein!
concepts.label: Creature_final_farewell

concepts.definition: The creature’s assertion that his agony and remorse surpassed Frankenstein’s wretchedness.
concepts.evidence_quote: Blasted as thou wert, my agony was still superior to thine, for the bitter sting of remorse will not cease to rankle in my wounds until death shall close them for ever.
concepts.label: Creature_comparison_of_suffering

concepts.label: ventilation_shafts

concepts.label: underground_machinery

concepts.label: arched_cavern

concepts.label: derelict_museum

concepts.label: technical_chemistry_gallery

concepts.label: narrator_friend

concepts.label: ArcticVoyageOfDiscovery

concepts.label: Weena

concepts.definition: A composite, partly comic dance the narrator performs on dusty museum flooring after acquiring matches, intended to delight Weena.
concepts.evidence_quote: And so, in that derelict museum, upon the thick soft carpeting of dust, to Weena’s huge delight, I solemnly performed a kind of composite dance, whistling _The Land of the Leal_ as cheerfully as I could.
concepts.label: Narrator_Celebratory_Dance

concepts.definition: The fixing and pulling of a lever on the time machine, which detaches clinging hands and returns the narrator to the grey light and tumult of time travel.
concepts.evidence_quote: “But at last the lever was fixed and pulled over. The clinging hands slipped from me. The darkness presently fell from my eyes.
concepts.label: Time_Machine_Lever_Action

concepts.definition: The peculiar visual and sensory environment the narrator experiences when engaged in time travel.
concepts.evidence_quote: I found myself in the same grey light and tumult I have already described.
concepts.label: Grey_Light_and_Tumult

concepts.definition: The Time Traveller’s workroom, entered via a corridor, whose door can be heard slamming when he goes in to perform some experiment.
concepts.evidence_quote: I heard the door of the laboratory slam, seated myself in a chair, and took up a daily paper.
concepts.label: Laboratory_Room

concepts.definition: A planned meeting between the narrator and Richardson the publisher, scheduled for two o’clock and nearly missed.
concepts.evidence_quote: Then suddenly I was reminded by an advertisement that I had promised to meet Richardson, the publisher, at two.
concepts.label: Narrator_Engagement_with_Richardson

concepts.definition: A sea expedition heading toward the North Pole, perceived as dangerous yet undertaken for exploration and discovery.
concepts.evidence_quote: I replied, however, that we were on a voyage of discovery towards the northern pole.
concepts.label: Arctic_voyage_of_discovery

concepts.definition: A man near death encountered in the Arctic, whose condition makes it surprising that he questions the value of rescue.
concepts.evidence_quote: You may conceive my astonishment on hearing such a question addressed to me from a man on the brink of destruction and to whom I should have supposed that my vessel would have been a resource which he would not have exchanged for the most precious wealth the earth can afford.
concepts.label: Shipwrecked_stranger_on_ice

concepts.definition: A particular day whose events are described as determining the narrator’s future destiny.
concepts.evidence_quote: Thus ended a day memorable to me; it decided my future destiny.
concepts.label: Fateful_decisive_day

concepts.definition: An exhortation to Victor to abandon thoughts of revenge and instead adopt peaceful, gentle feelings toward others while grieving.
concepts.evidence_quote: “Come, Victor; not brooding thoughts of vengeance against the assassin, but with feelings of peace and gentleness, that will heal, instead of festering, the wounds of our minds.
concepts.label: Call_for_peace_over_vengeance

concepts.definition: A home marked by recent loss and grief, which Victor is urged to enter with kindness and affection rather than hatred.
concepts.evidence_quote: Enter the house of mourning, my friend, but with kindness and affection for those who love you, and not with hatred for your enemies.
concepts.label: House_of_mourning

concepts.definition: A stance that refuses consent to the death of any human, even while judging some people unfit for human society.
concepts.evidence_quote: I could not consent to the death of any human being, but certainly I should have thought such a creature unfit to remain in the society of men.
concepts.label: Moral_rejection_of_execution

concepts.definition: The speaker’s intense conviction that Justine is innocent, supported by Victor’s agreement.
concepts.evidence_quote: But she was innocent. I know, I feel she was innocent; you are of the same opinion, and that confirms me.
concepts.label: Belief_in_Justine_innocence

concepts.definition: The anxiety that arises when lies are so similar to truth that they threaten one’s sense of secure happiness.
concepts.evidence_quote: Alas! Victor, when falsehood can look so like the truth, who can assure themselves of certain happiness?
concepts.label: Falsehood_resembling_truth_fear

concepts.definition: A metaphor of walking on the edge of a precipice, with crowds trying to push the speaker into an abyss, expressing extreme emotional peril.
concepts.evidence_quote: I feel as if I were walking on the edge of a precipice, towards which thousands are crowding and endeavouring to plunge me into the abyss.
concepts.label: Precipice_of_despair_image

concepts.definition: The still-free killer responsible for the deaths of William and Justine, who is imagined as walking the world unpunished and perhaps respected.
concepts.evidence_quote: William and Justine were assassinated, and the murderer escapes; he walks about the world free, and perhaps respected.
concepts.label: Unpunished_murderer_of_William_and_Justine

concepts.definition: The speaker’s belief that even dying on the scaffold for the same crimes would be preferable to being the murderer, called a wretch.
concepts.evidence_quote: But even if I were condemned to suffer on the scaffold for the same crimes, I would not change places with such a wretch.”
concepts.label: Moral_superiority_over_wretch

concepts.definition: The process by which the creature learns spoken language and written letters, opening a new domain of wonder and delight.
concepts.evidence_quote: “While I improved in speech, I also learned the science of letters as it was taught to the stranger, and this opened before me a wide field for wonder and delight.
concepts.label: Creature_literary_education

concepts.definition: The creature’s practice of traveling only at night, driven by fear of human faces and enduring severe environmental hardship.
concepts.evidence_quote: I travelled only at night, fearful of encountering the visage of a human being. Nature decayed around me, and the sun became heatless; rain and snow poured around me; mighty rivers were frozen;
concepts.label: Creature_night_travel_and_isolation

concepts.definition: The creature’s expressed hatred toward whatever caused his existence, associated with a change from mildness to bitterness.
concepts.evidence_quote: Oh, earth! How often did I imprecate curses on the cause of my being! The mildness of my nature had fled, and all within me was turned to gall and bitterness.
concepts.label: Creature_curse_on_cause_of_being

concepts.definition: The intense revengeful feeling that grows as the creature approaches Victor’s dwelling.
concepts.evidence_quote: The nearer I approached to your habitation, the more deeply did I feel the spirit of revenge enkindled in my heart.
concepts.label: Creature_spirit_of_revenge

concepts.definition: A journey where the creature uses occasional incidents and a map for direction, yet frequently strays from the path.
concepts.evidence_quote: A few incidents now and then directed me, and I possessed a map of the country; but I often wandered wide from my path.
concepts.label: Creature_guided_yet_errant_journey

concepts.definition: A characterization of a traveller’s life as blending considerable pain with its pleasures, with perpetual emotional strain.
concepts.evidence_quote: But he found that a traveller’s life is one that includes much pain amidst its enjoyments. His feelings are for ever on the stretch;
concepts.label: Traveller_life_dual_pain_and_enjoyment

concepts.definition: The traveller’s forced abandonment of each new pleasure for another novelty, preventing lasting repose.
concepts.evidence_quote: and when he begins to sink into repose, he finds himself obliged to quit that on which he rests in pleasure for something new, which again engages his attention, and which also he forsakes for other novelties.
concepts.label: Restlessness_of_traveller

concepts.definition: Mr. Kirwin’s interpretive response to Victor’s exclamation as a sign of guilt, expressed with a troubled and severe manner.
concepts.evidence_quote: Mr. Kirwin regarded me with a troubled countenance. He could not help regarding my exclamation as a presumption of my guilt and said in rather a severe tone,
concepts.label: Mr_Kirwin_suspicion_of_Victor

concepts.definition: The creature’s description of revenge as both a vice and the consuming, solitary passion dominating his soul.
concepts.evidence_quote: My revenge is of no moment to you; yet, while I allow it to be a vice, I confess that it is the devouring and only passion of my soul.
concepts.label: Creature_devouring_passion_of_revenge

concepts.definition: The creature’s furious reflection that the murderer he released into society still lives, intensifying his rage.
concepts.evidence_quote: My rage is unspeakable when I reflect that the murderer, whom I have turned loose upon society, still exists.
concepts.label: Creature_self_blame_for_murderer

concepts.definition: The creature’s vow to devote his life or death to destroying the murderer after his request is refused.
concepts.evidence_quote: You refuse my just demand; I have but one resource, and I devote myself, either in my life or death, to his destruction.”
concepts.label: Creature_self_dedication_to_destruction_pursuit

concepts.definition: The creature’s declaration that Frankenstein is the last human he will ever see, as part of his final farewell.
concepts.evidence_quote: “Farewell! I leave you, and in you the last of humankind whom these eyes will ever behold. Farewell, Frankenstein!
concepts.label: Creature_final_farewell_to_humankind

concepts.definition: The creature’s assertion that his agony, heightened by remorse, surpassed Frankenstein’s suffering.
concepts.evidence_quote: Blasted as thou wert, my agony was still superior to thine, for the bitter sting of remorse will not cease to rankle in my wounds until death shall close them for ever.
concepts.label: Creature_comparison_of_suffering_with_Frankenstein

concepts.definition: The claim that Frankenstein sought the creature’s extinction so that he would not cause greater misery.
concepts.evidence_quote: But it was not so; thou didst seek my extinction, that I might not cause greater wretchedness;
concepts.label: Frankenstein_attempt_to_prevent_further_wretchedness
